title: fix(cron): prevent announce wakes from resetting CLI chats
body:
Fixes #176208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an announce cron wake targeting an existing chat discards its native CLI conversation, and the next chat turn discards it again with `reason=message-policy`.

## User Impact

Scheduled wakes and subsequent replies retain the chat's CLI binding. Announce turns still require explicit message targets, and isolated/current cron runs retain their existing delivery policy. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cron producer now derives persistent-session binding facts from the same `resolveSessionStableReplyMode` owner as chat and heartbeat turns. Preparation and execution share those facts; cron-specific targeting remains a per-turn restriction. The strict CLI fingerprint comparator is unchanged, so genuine policy changes still invalidate bindings.

Original fix by @eliavb43; maintainer cleanup consolidates duplicate binding construction, reuses the admitted runtime's metadata snapshot, replaces argument-shape assertions with actual CLI preparation/reuse checks, and documents the behavior.

The background run carries admitted config/metadata and the prepared session identity under its existing runtime lease and serialized session lifecycle. This change adds no new detached side effect, path, limit, or authorization capture; existing execution and settlement authority checks remain in force.

## Evidence

- Source/history confirmation: main still constructs announce binding facts with `requireExplicitMessageTarget: true`, while ordinary chat uses the stable session policy. `prepareCliRunContext` hashes those facts and `resolveCliSessionReuse` invalidates the mismatch. The earlier direct-command continuity fix (#164378) preserves strict policy comparison and establishes the shared-policy precedent.
- Regression cases in `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts`: `preserves the chat CLI binding across an announce wake` and `preserves the isolated CLI binding across an announce wake`. Cron-produced facts flow through real CLI preparation/reuse across ordinary → announce → ordinary turns; targeting remains explicit on the wake. The chat case would reach `invalidate:message-policy` without the fix. Baseline execution was intentionally not run.
- Local formatting: `oxfmt --check` passed on all five changed files. Changed-file oxlint passed with the core tsconfig and every applicable repository rule; the shared install lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`, so the temporary config omits only its unrelated `ui/**` override. No dependencies were installed.
- Autoreview: pre-commit and final committed-branch reviews both `scoped-clean` at P0–P2, with no actionable findings. The final review included CLI preparation/reuse and fixture source context.
- Exact-head PR CI is the test gate: it covers the selected core/cron test shards, typechecks, static checks, and applicable build/integration jobs. [CI run 39164049117](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39164049117) passed for head `fccbd04245cfacbd857ce170851ca14c64f9f29f`: 36 successful jobs, zero failures; `openclaw/ci-gate`, production/test types, lint, selected tests, docs, and security checks are green.
- Live Gateway/Claude CLI proof, leases, local tests/typechecks, and production-only negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy (2026-10-13: “relax testing and trust PR CI, just lint”). No live or warm-process proof is claimed. [ClawSweeper's exact-head re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176218#issuecomment-6250842204) reports zero findings, removes the prior proof-only hold, and marks the PR ready for maintainer review; the call-shape test concern is addressed above.
- Test cost: two cases and six in-process CLI preparations, with no CLI subprocess, network calls, sleeps, or polling added. Local wall time was intentionally not measured. [CI job 117783481887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39164049117/job/117783481887) passed the complete file (16/16 tests): chat regression 1.736s, isolated regression 0.757s, Vitest duration 10.67s, wrapper wall time 12.04s.
- Diff versus main: production +22/-10 (net +12), tests +98/-0, docs +3/-1. The necessary growth selects stable policy once at the producer and forwards one shared result; unrelated deletion would not improve this fix.
